title: Optimal Dose for Factor Activity Screening at High Signal-to-Noise Ratio
banked_reason: The proposal expressly requires finite-SNR optimizer uniqueness and complete transition topology as outputs, but the core retains those branches, ties, and transition conditions as an open question and supplies only a partial topology result.
gap_reasons: The proposal expressly requires finite-SNR optimizer uniqueness and complete transition topology as outputs, but the core retains those branches, ties, and transition conditions as an open question and supplies only a partial topology result.
This is a partial topology result; it does not determine the number of global branches, finite-signal ties, or transition values.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery discharged the sharp first-order high-signal information frontier, all-randomized-design converse, uniform overlap remainder, every-maximizer localization, and a finite certified-computation procedure; the math referee passed the resulting note. The original contract also required finite-signal optimizer uniqueness and transition topology, but the solver left the complete branch/tie/transition correspondence open and supplied only partial topology, which the rubric and two independent consultations classified as terminal kernel substitution. The narrower sound package was assessed incremental below the field floor; formalization was not started, and no Lean theorem was verified.
tldr: Activity screening selects factors with nonzero causal endpoint effects. In the fixed two-factor Bernoulli--Gaussian experiment, the proposed sharp theorem gives an optimum approaching \(\frac32\log2\), with first deficit \(\frac{\sqrt2}{12\sqrt\pi}s^{-1/4}(\log s)^{3/2}\), and localizes every maximizing squared-dose ratio at \(u\sim\frac12s^{-1/2}\). Its analytic kernel is a uniform weighted-overlap expansion that retains the information between the two merging high-variance labels. Endpoint exclusions and Gaussian garbling supply the global converse for every recorded randomized law. A terminating interval-quadrature procedure supplies finite-signal optimum brackets; complete finite-signal branch and tie topology is an explicit open question.
gap: Sparse Bayesian screening and noncoherent model discrimination already supply activity information, scalar mixture integrals, gradients, and power separation. The inspected literature does not supply the simultaneous fixed-fair-label, real one-observation, peak-dose frontier with its sharp deficit and every-maximizer localization.
fill: The proposed theorem joins a weighted real-Gaussian overlap coefficient to a two-parameter remainder, global endpoint exclusion, a constructive dose, and an all-law upper certificate. Finite-signal computation carries explicit analytic and outward-rounding error budgets. The contribution is a specialized subfield controlled-screening result.
